newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta paper mill expected to be announced Monday.
newsitem.headline: Alberta paper mill expected to be announced Monday.

text.p: The Canadian province of Alberta is expected to announce on Monday the go-ahead for long-delayed C$900 million pulp and paper mill, the chairman of the company formed to operate the plant said on Friday.
"There's going to be a government announcement Monday," James Hole, chairman of Grande Alberta Paper Ltd, said in an interview. "Monday the whole story will be there."
Hole said the announcement would detail the first phase of the project, which he described as a lightweight, coated paper mill with a pulp component.

Grande Alberta for four years has planned the mill, to be built in the town of Grande Prarie, Alberta. The delay was reportedly caused by financial concerns over the project and a dispute over the amount of government-owned timber lands to be allocated.
The mill has been scaled down from an original C$1.6-billion proposal and the Alberta government earlier this week gave approval to the plant's timber allocation.
Hole said he would not disclose the corporate affiliations of the consortium's three principal shareholders until Monday's announcement. He added that financing came from their "personal companies."
The environmental and regulatory process was expected to take 18-24 months and the projject could create 285 permanent and 150 seasonal jobs. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
